content: A Russian SU-27 Flanker fighter jet engaged in an aggressive maneuver towards a US RC-135U intelligence-gathering plane in international airspace over the Sea of Okhotsk on April 23, amid heightened tensions between the US and Russia over Ukraine.
Charles, the Prince of Wales, and his wife Camilla will embark on a 12-day tour of Australia and New Zealand, visiting 12 towns and cities, including meeting the new Australian PM Malcolm Turnbull.
A man has been detained and is being questioned by police in Killarney, Ireland, in connection with a September attack on a woman in Sneem, County Kerry.
Former GP Hugh McGoldrick's name will be erased from the medical register after he failed to appeal the Medical Practitioners Tribunal's ruling within the 28-day deadline.
A 21-year-old male is being held on suspicion of murder by Surrey Police, who are awaiting the results of a post-mortem examination after a man was found in a wooded area near Dorking.
A 21-year-old man, Josh Hanson, was stabbed to death at a bar in Eastcote, London, and Scotland Yard is urging around 40 people who were present at the time to come forward with information.

Hovertravel, a cross-Solent service provider, is considering adding a new service between Sandown and Southsea, operating on Tuesdays and Thursdays in July and August, in an effort to boost tourism on the Isle of Wight.
A 30-year-old man was arrested and later released on bail after a victim was attacked by up to eight men in the Heights area on Sunday.

In India, the death toll from recent floods has doubled to over 200 after waters receded, affecting 450,000 people, with the government announcing aid packages and the Prime Minister set to visit the affected state of Assam.

Arsenal will host Leicester City on Friday 11 August, marking the start of the Premier League's 25th anniversary season, with Sky Sports set to broadcast the match as part of their Friday night fixtures.
Oldham Athletic Football Club has dismissed Cristian Montano, a 22-year-old player who was arrested in an investigation into spot-fixing, after a thorough investigation by the club.

A 20-year-old man, Rick Edwards, was given a suspended 12-month jail term and a year's supervision order after admitting to starting a fire at the former Pontins resort in Brixham in 2014, stating he did it "for fun".
Wilson, a 30-year-old footballer, has been without a team since being released in May, after making 51 appearances in his second spell at Nottingham Forest.
Australia won the second one-day international against Sri Lanka by 82 runs, levelling the five-match series at 1-1, after restricting Sri Lanka to 288 and then scoring 206 in reply.
Sale Sharks' forward Vadim Cobilas has signed with French Top 14 team Bordeaux, becoming the latest player to leave the Premiership club this summer.

India, led by a 212-run partnership between Shikhar Dhawan and Virat Kohli, collapsed from a promising position to be bowled out for 323, despite their duo both making hundreds, as Australia won the match by 25 runs and took a 4-0 lead in the five-match series.
The Hammersmith and City Line and parts of the Circle Line have been suspended due to concerns over debris from a 24-storey block fire in London, which has led to a presumed 58 deaths.
Jamie Hamill, a 27-year-old player who previously played for Kilmarnock and Hearts, has signed a three-year contract to return to Kilmarnock, making his second debut for the club.

During a match between Ipswich and Norwich, a fan named Ross Morgan accidentally punched a hole in his ceiling while celebrating a goal, and the goal-scorer, Paul Anderson, later offered to pay for the repairs.
In Wales, a new law requires retailers to keep cigarettes out of public view, with shop managers and assistants facing fines of up to £5,000 and prison for non-compliance.

Bristol Rovers has signed 20-year-old Lucas, who has previously played for the National League side and scored three goals in 10 appearances, to add options in the forward areas of their League Two squad.

Network Rail is undertaking maintenance work at Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire, including making the station watertight and rebuilding the chimney stack, while minimizing disruption by carrying out some work at night.

Lawrence Phillips, a former NFL player and convicted felon, was found dead in a cell, with officials believing he took his own life, despite being accused of killing his former cellmate and having a history of trouble with the law.
The Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) plan proposes extending bus lane operating hours from 07:30 to 19:00, with potential flexibility and community input through two rounds of consultation.
Lionel Messi scored the winning goal for Barcelona in their La Liga match against Atletico, becoming the competition's all-time top scorer with 287 goals.

In a major match-fixing scandal, over 70 people, including players and directors from around 30 clubs in Italy's lower divisions, are under investigation and more than 70 are detained, with some suspected links to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate.

Approximately 1,600 Dolomedes plantarius spiderlings, bred as hybrids between species from Sussex and Suffolk, have been released into a dyke at Castle Marshes to help establish a new population with increased genetic diversity and adaptability to climate change.
In 2017, the article refers to the Partition of India, a historical event where two new countries gained independence from British rule, resulting in millions of people becoming refugees.

Iva Barr, a 30-year marathon veteran who participated in the first London Marathon in 1981, completed about 14 miles of the course before walking the final part to the finish line, calling the experience "wonderful" despite not finishing in a traditional sense.

In China's top cities, the high demand for property has led to couples undergoing fake divorces to buy additional homes, as the central bank's efforts to curb rising prices have failed to alleviate the struggles of low-wage young workers.
A 46-year-old landlord, Mr Jones, died at a public house in Holyhead, and a 24-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a stand-off with police.

A fatal car crash occurred on the A713 near Carsphairn, Scotland, when a red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided, resulting in the deaths of both drivers, a 50-year-old man and a 46-year-old man from Ayrshire.

Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in the women's pair in 2012, was a strong inspiration to many young athletes due to her determination and personality, despite being diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013.

A series of bombings in Afghanistan, including one that destroyed an army bus in western Kabul, injured several people and killed at least 15, with the Taliban claiming responsibility for the attacks.

Daimler, the parent company of Mercedes-Benz, reported a 6% increase in sales of its cars and commercial vehicles in the second quarter, with the company confident that its full-year sales will exceed 100 billion euros despite a slowdown in sales in China.

A 10-year-old son of Danish Crown Prince Frederik was saved by a lifeguard, Nick Malcolm, at Mermaid Beach after being caught in a rip current, with officials initially downplaying the incident but later acknowledging the potential severity of the situation.
A fire at a property on Elgin Road in Scotland resulted in the discovery of an elderly man's body, with police indicating that there are no suspicious circumstances.

Veterans with amputation-related medical issues can now access specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) in Surrey, following a new program aimed at providing the best possible care for those who have made significant sacrifices for Britain's safety.

In Port Talbot, four speed cameras have caught around 125 drivers per day in their first week of operation, with the partnership behind the cameras noting a decrease in the number of drivers exceeding the speed limit compared to a previous trial period.

A Manchester-born teacher, arrested in Valladolid, Spain, as part of an Interpol investigation, is suspected of possessing and sharing sexually explicit files involving minors, including secretly taking photos of his students.

A sturgeon named Steve, who escaped from a water centre in Romsey, Hampshire due to flooding, has been found in a nearby car wash a mile away, where he was discovered in a deep puddle and is reportedly "only a little worse for wear" after his ordeal.
Comedian Chris Rock has filed for divorce from his wife, Malaak Compton-Rock, after 19 years of marriage, with the couple having two daughters together.
A multi-vehicle collision on the motorway at Tamnamore, near junctions 13 and 14, has caused the road to be closed in both directions, resulting in significant traffic congestion.

The French government has nominated senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini as ambassador to the Vatican, but the Vatican has yet to respond, with observers interpreting the long silence as a potential rejection.

The Nasdaq index experienced its largest one-day decline since April 10 last year, falling 2.4% or 118 points to 4,876, despite a significant gain in Kraft Foods shares following a merger announcement.
Marketa Vondrousova won her first WTA title by defeating Anett Kontaveit 6-4 7-6 (8-6), and Borna Coric also won his first ATP title by saving five match points to defeat Philipp Kohlschreiber.
Stoke City has signed 28-year-old Eric Choupo-Moting, their fourth summer signing, who has played for various European clubs and has represented Cameroon in 48 international caps.

A 56-year-old man, Seamus McCollum, who had cerebral palsy and lived in a Maine private nursing home, was treated as a murder victim only after an autopsy in April, nearly six months after his death in September.

Heavy rains triggered by a depression in the Bay of Bengal have brought Chennai to a standstill, forced the closure of many offices and schools, and displaced thousands of people, with the government announcing a relief fund of 5 billion rupees.
A bus caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road near Largs on Saturday, but thanks to the driver's quick actions, all passengers, including a partially-sighted woman and her mother, escaped uninjured.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old English cricketer, has made a strong start to the 2016 County Championship season, taking six wickets in each of Notts' first two games and impressing his team with his performance with the new ball.

A memorial stone, made from Jersey granite, has been unveiled in the French village of Guillemont to commemorate the role of Jersey in World War I, with a core of the stone to be returned to Jersey to be part of a monument in Royal Square.

John Boyega, who played Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens, has visited his former theatre company, Theatre Peckham, where he was a member from age nine to 14, and expressed his desire to give back to the organization.
England's Luke Donald carded a 65, with six birdies in nine holes, moving him four strokes behind the leaders, Aphibarnrat and Fitzpatrick, at the European Tour event.

Middlesex ended day one of their County Championship match against Hampshire in a strong position, with Adam Voges unbeaten on 128 and the hosts having reached 342-3, thanks in part to a 279-run partnership between Voges and Dawid Malan.

A 52-year-old woman has died and a 16-year-old boy is in critical condition after an incident in Penilee Road, with a 54-year-old man, who was initially sought by police, now located in the Dumfries and Galloway area.

A three-bedroom house in Wavertree, where a young member of The Beatles lived from birth until age five, has been sold to an anonymous telephone bidder after a "bidding war" at a price likely between £150,000 and £250,000.

A 29-year-old man, Aaron Joseph, has denied being the owner of a dog that caused injury while being dangerously out of control, in connection with the death of a 52-year-old man, David Ellam, who was attacked while walking his dog in Huddersfield last August.
A 22-year-old man from Shrewsbury, Thomas Bebbington, was last seen entering a river on November 10 and a body was found on private land near Leighton about 10 miles away from the city center.
Five-week-old baby otters are doing well but still require six daily feeds, with plans to eventually move them to an outdoor enclosure with a pool and feed them live food by summer.
Police in Newtownards are seeking witnesses to a bonfire disturbance and potential activity around the home of 33-year-old Joanne Thompson, who was found deceased on Wednesday.
A record-breaking 2,270 black-tailed godwits were spotted on the island of Tiree this spring, with many stopping to refuel before their migration to Iceland.

Former Rangers player and coach, Ian Durrant, will not be returning to the club after spending last season as the Under-20 development squad manager, as Rangers manager Mark Warburton is looking to make changes to the coaching personnel.
A rare albino deer has drawn attention from visitors, with biologists estimating that such births occur only once every 100,000.

A 13-year-old boy, Asad Khan, died three weeks after starting at a school in Bradford, with his family claiming he had been bullied, and the inquest is ongoing to investigate the circumstances surrounding his death.

A unique painting, believed to have been created before 1880, depicting the 1654 coronation ceremony, has been restored and is now being investigated by experts to determine its origins, with its current owner, Sir Andrew Morritt, seeking to uncover how it ended up at Rokeby Park in Durham.
Macclesfield Town secured a 3-0 victory over Wrexham, with Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whitaker scoring for the visitors.

French oil and gas company Total has partnered with the Confederation of African Football (Caf) as the new headline sponsor for 10 competitions, including the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations finals in Gabon.
Spain has announced a 23-player squad for their upcoming friendly against Belgium and World Cup qualifier against Liechtenstein, with several players recalled, including Diego Costa and Juan Mata.

A large wildfire, believed to have been started deliberately, has spread across a 5-kilometre area, with 45 firefighters and eight appliances at the scene, as part of a growing concern with 435 reported wildfires since May.
Former England and Ireland cricketer Boyd Rankin has made a comeback to Ireland, citing the opportunity to be part of the country's potential bid for Test status as a major draw.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, created with the Patient Client Council, aims to provide an independent voice and improve treatment and care for individuals and families affected by rare diseases in Northern Ireland.

Gloucester Cathedral is introducing girl choristers to its choir, established by Henry VIII in 1539, with the aim of discovering talented young girls from local schools and backgrounds to join the cathedral's musical worship.
Pedro, a 29-year-old Chelsea winger, was hospitalized after suffering a head injury in a game, but has since been released and is expected to return to training with a protective mask.

Nottinghamshire has appointed former England cricketer James Taylor as a batting coach, and former Northants captain David Sales will also work with the county's batsmen, bringing their respective experiences to the team.
A man has been charged with several offenses, including assault on police, after an incident on Whiterock Road in Belfast, and is due to appear in court on December 5.
A volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI successfully towed a yacht to Carrick Marina after its engine failed in good weather conditions.
Ipswich Town secured a 3-2 win over MK Dons, with goals from David McGoldrick, Brett Pitman, and Varney, despite MK Dons leveling twice through Revell.

A man from Darlington has been issued a summons to appear in court on charges of dangerous driving and causing serious injury after a bridge collapsed onto a London-bound carriageway of the M25 motorway on August 27, injuring a motorcyclist.

A group of approximately 200 people, organized on social media, staged a flashmob in the Costa Brava town of Platja d'Aro, where they pretended to be paparazzi chasing a celebrity, causing panic and a stampede among bystanders.

A 2.5-year-old boy, Jeremiah Regis, was found with over 100 injuries, including a bite to the chest, and died from abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma, leading to the murder charges against his mother, Sindyann Regis, and her partner, Chevaze Mcgregor.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common has engulfed a significant area, with 20 fire engine crews battling the flames and one person taken to hospital with burns, as firefighters face challenges with wind direction and water supplies.
The British Speedway Promoters' Association has announced an agreement to keep Leicester Speedway club going, with a 15-year lease also signed for its Beaumont Park venue.
A 50-year-old woman, Elizabeth Bowe, died three days after being found badly injured at her home in St Andrews, and her 51-year-old brother, Charles Gordon, has been charged with her murder.
Ross County has signed 29-year-old midfielder Jim O'Brien on a two-year contract, bringing him back to the club on a permanent deal after a successful six-month loan spell last season.
Northants' seam attack took advantage of Durham's fragile batting line-up, restricting the visitors to 59-3, 107 runs behind, before Northants' own batting was halted due to bad light.

New Zealand's Ko, a 19-year-old, is one shot behind joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim after two rounds at the Sahalee Country Club in Seattle, with five players under par at the halfway stage of the second women's major of the year.
Gordon Watson, a 56-year-old former coach, has joined Scotland's national team as an assistant to manager Gordon Strachan, marking his second stint with the team.

The Belfast Giants secured a 5-3 win over the Cardiff Devils, with Colin Shields scoring the first goal and the Giants ultimately taking control through second-period goals from Ryan Martinelli and Mark Garside.
Danny Willett won the Masters, becoming the first Englishman to do so since Nick Faldo in 1996, after Jordan Spieth suffered a quadruple-bogey and collapsed from a five-shot lead on the final day.

The BBC's England's Big Picture invites viewers to share their photos by emailing them to england@bbc.co.uk, posting on social media, or using a specific hashtag, with guidelines including copyright ownership and a royalty-free license for the BBC to use the submitted images.

An optometrist, Honey Rose, is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter after allegedly failing to detect a life-threatening condition during a routine eye test, which led to the death of a patient, Vincent Barker, five months later.

China's food price inflation rose to 4.9% in June, a figure above analysts' expectations but still below the government's target, which may reduce the likelihood of interest rate cuts and suggests a neutral monetary policy.
Ivory Coast international Tiote, a former Newcastle player, died after collapsing during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on June 5.
Slovak Peter Sagan won the fifth stage of the Tour de France, with Thibaut Pinot moving into second place overall behind leader Nairo Quintana.

Cuadrilla's plans for fracking at its Preston New Road site in Lancashire have been approved, despite a pending legal challenge, with the company promising to prioritize job creation, skills development, and community investment in the region.

Three teenage males from north-west London, who were feared to be traveling to Syria, were arrested by Turkish officials at Istanbul's airport after flying in from Barcelona, and were later released without charge by UK police.

A respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital, Dr Christopher Davies, questioned the £22.95 cost of a blackout blind purchased from Homebase, suggesting that the price may not be justified, despite the hospital stating that the quote was reviewed and rejected.
The Swansea City development squad celebrated a successful 2016-17 season, winning the cup final and achieving 31 wins across all competitions, following their senior team's Premier League survival.

Denbighshire councillors are considering creating a secondary dune system at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn to strengthen defences and reduce the risk of flooding, following severe storms in December 2013.
South Shields will host a special FA Cup match on August 19, with commentary by Conor McNamara and Danny Webber, and the game will be streamed live across BBC Sport's digital platforms.

Police in Scotland are investigating a targeted attack on a property in which a 38-year-old man suffered serious facial injuries and a 49-year-old man was not injured, with officers seeking information from witnesses and potential vehicle sightings.
Pamela McLaggan pleaded guilty to manslaughter after Jonathan Baines, also known as "Willy", was found dead at a house in Gainsborough, with prosecutors accepting her plea.
A 15-year-old boy was assaulted at Patterton station on October 3, suffering facial injuries, after being punched and stamped by a man and woman in their 40s, and his mobile phone was stolen.

Two 17-year-old boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, are being investigated by West Yorkshire Police and counter-terrorism officers for allegedly traveling to Syria to join the Islamic State in March.

The Great Britain ice hockey team has announced a 22-man squad for the upcoming 2018 Winter Games qualifying tournament, featuring several experienced players including Jonathan Boxill, Craig Peacock, and Colin Shields.
Matthew Perry, a former star of the popular sitcom "Friends," may make a brief appearance in a tribute special to the show's creator James Burrows, but it's not a reunion episode.
Jones, a 31-year-old player who started his career at Manchester United, made 41 league appearances for Burnley last season, helping them win the Championship title.
A lawyer, Joe Acquaro, was found shot dead in Melbourne, and investigators suspect that underworld figures may have put a price on his head due to his representation of crime bosses.

Air France flight AF374, carrying 294 passengers from Paris to Vancouver, was diverted to Glasgow Prestwick after a slight smell of burning was detected on board, and passengers were later flown back to Charles de Gaulle Airport on a second aircraft.
The remains of Hurricane Gonzalo are expected to bring strong winds and heavy rain to Britain, particularly coastal areas and north-western Wales, with the worst weather forecast for Tuesday.
People are concerned that overcrowding in hospitals is causing long wait times for patients, including children who need medical attention.

A 64-year-old man, Kenneth David Dickie, has died from a serious head injury sustained in Poole, and two individuals, a 34-year-old man and a 57-year-old woman, have been charged and bailed in connection with the incident.
Former Manchester United forward Matteo Macheda will stay at Nottingham Forest's City Ground until the end of the season, having joined on a deal that included a 24-hour recall clause.

The body of Christopher Huxtable, a 34-year-old man from Swansea who had been missing since a building collapse in February, was finally found, with his family able to gain closure, while two other men, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, remain missing.
Bristol City head coach Lee Johnson emphasizes the importance of a win against QPR, which could significantly improve their position in the league and draw other teams into the competition.

Italian astronaut Luca described walking in space as "absolutely fantastic" after his 2013 mission to the International Space Station, where he participated in two spacewalks and traveled over 110 million kilometers.
Joe Arundel, a former England Knights player, has joined Hull FC, a new club, after making 44 first-team appearances and scoring 16 tries for his previous team.

Ulster Bank, a subsidiary of RBS, is working to resolve an issue affecting approximately 600,000 customer payments, which it aims to update by Saturday, with the bank assuring customers that they will not be left out of pocket as a result of the issue.
Tanzania secured a 2-1 win over Kenya in the 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, while Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1 in a separate third-place play-off match.

Due to industrial action in America, McDonald's Japan is rationing French fries by serving only small portions, as the company struggles to obtain enough potatoes, with imports expected to alleviate the shortage in January.

The total purse for the Derby on June 3 has increased to £1.625m due to the addition of new entrants, with John Gosden-trained Cracksman as the favourite, while trainer John Jenkins is defending the decision to run long-shot filly Diore Lia.
Atletico Madrid's top scorer, Antoine Griezmann, has suffered a haematoma on his left foot, but an X-ray has ruled out a bone injury, forcing him to miss France's friendly against Ivory Coast.
Veteran rugby league prop Willie Mason has joined the Dragons in Super League, bringing a wealth of experience from his 15-year career, including 290 NRL games and 24 tests for the Kangaroos.
A survey by The Marine Conservation Society found an 11% increase in dog mess on UK beaches overall, with a 71% increase in Scotland, but also reported a decrease in overall litter levels.

The UK Supreme Court ruled that the government's introduction of court fees in 2013 was unlawful and unconstitutional, as it indirectly discriminated against women by making it more expensive for them to pursue discrimination cases.
Wycombe won the match against Dagenham & Redbridge, moving up to sixth spot in the league, while Dagenham remain in the relegation places.
Bee-eaters, a native European species, have successfully bred at Low Gelt Quarry in the UK for a second consecutive summer, with chicks expected to fledge in the next few weeks.

A boy jumped into the River Wey in Guildford to try and save his father after their boat capsized, but was advised by members of the public to return, and a search is currently underway for the missing kayaker.

A girl visiting Rabat Zoo in Morocco was fatally struck by a stone thrown by an elephant, with the zoo stating that the incident was rare and unpredictable, despite meeting international safety standards.

Labour MP Laura Glass has been appointed to the shadow cabinet, replacing Emma Powell, who resigned citing that Jeremy Corbyn's position as party leader had become "untenable" due to concerns over his ability to provide an effective opposition.
Chelsea manager Conte believes six teams, including Chelsea, Tottenham, and Manchester United, have a strong chance to win the title with 14 games remaining in the top flight.

A dispersal order has been issued in Llangefni, allowing police and community support officers to force troublemakers to leave the area and take measures to protect both residents and young people from anti-social behavior and the potential consequences of excessive alcohol consumption.
Boro's manager Garry Monk has confirmed an interest in signing Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker, while the club has also seen the departure of De Roon, who played 33 Premier League games last season.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, established in 2008 to recognize humorous children's books, is set to be relaunched in 2016 as part of Roald Dahl's centenary celebrations with the goal of ensuring a "robust future" for the award.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr., a 74-year-old white supremacist, was sentenced to death by lethal injection for the murders of three people at Jewish sites in Kansas, after being convicted of capital murder and other charges.

A city council plans to introduce a large-scale self-service bike scheme, with 500 bikes located across the city from April 2017, and aims to secure a provider to operate the scheme at no cost to taxpayers.

West Ham's Diafra Sakho has returned to light training after back surgery and is essentially starting his own pre-season training schedule, requiring time to regain sufficient fitness levels before being considered for selection.
In Northern Ireland, property prices rose by 5.4% annually in the third quarter, with the average standardised price reaching £124,000, while the quarterly increase was minimal at 0.8%.

A recent delivery of a giant wind turbine part on the A713 in Dumfries and Galloway ended in a lorry and its cargo ending up in a ditch, highlighting the challenges of transporting large items on country roads.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is considering downgrading services at two of its district hospitals due to staffing shortages, but is facing opposition from residents who are concerned about the impact on local maternity care.
Mignon du Preez scored 116 off 99 balls as South Africa secured a 68-run win over Ireland in the second ODI, after the Irish were bowled out for 204 in response to South Africa's 272-6.

Peake, a 30-year-old athlete, is targeting a personal best and Welsh record at the Cardiff International Sports Stadium, with the goal of meeting the 4.50m qualification standard set by British Athletics for the Rio Olympics.
A fire that burned for over 10 hours at a building site in Llanwern, Wales, is believed to have been deliberately set, with police investigating the circumstances.
A charity event was held in Edinburgh to raise money for the Nepal earthquake relief effort, organized by Mercy Corps with the help of the Nepal Scotland Association and the city council.

Uefa has imposed a suspension on Hibernian head coach Neil Lennon for "acts of violence against the referee" during a Europa League qualifying match, and the club has announced that they are appealing the decision.

A fire broke out at the ICL UK Boulby mine, one of Europe's deepest mines, on April 13, resulting in seven workers being hospitalized for smoke inhalation and a notice being served by the Health and Safety Executive for the company to improve procedures.

Two men, including a 23-year-old British tourist, were removed from Machu Picchu in Peru after being caught posing naked by surveillance workers, and the British Foreign Office is in contact with local authorities regarding the incident.
Croatian international Ivan Rakitic is set to sign a new deal with Barcelona on Friday, reportedly worth a £109m buyout clause.

A couple from Halstead suffered "life-changing" injuries during a two-hour home invasion on April 26, and police are working to identify the suspects, who fled with a quantity of cash after threatening to harm the couple's family members.

The Wickerman Festival, taking place on July 25-26 near Dundrennan, has announced its lineup, including Dizzee Rascal as the opening night headliner, alongside other acts such as Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, and Big Country.
Foden, a 26-year-old rugby player, expressed hope that his performance and that of his Saints team could lead to a strong England rugby squad for the upcoming Six Nations tournament.
A 22-year-old motorcyclist died after a collision involving a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, with a 10-year-old boy in the car remaining in serious condition.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, the developer of the eczema cream crisaborole, which is awaiting US FDA approval and could potentially generate $2 billion in annual sales.
Police in Dagenham arrested two teenage boys, aged 17 and 15, after a street fight on Saturday, recovering three large knives, scissors, and cannabis from the scene.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff has been arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after a 19-year-old woman was reportedly attacked near Cardiff Civic Centre.

A by-election is to be held in the Berwickshire, Roxburgh and Selkirk constituency in Scotland, following the resignation of Conservative MSP John Lamont, who is seeking to unseat SNP MP Calum Kerr in a closely contested Westminster seat.

The European Union, including major beef-producing countries like France and Germany, has gained access to sell beef to Canada, a welcome move for EU farmers who are facing a difficult period due to export declines.

European finance ministers have endorsed plans to create a single EU list of "non-cooperative jurisdictions" by the end of the summer, following the Panama Papers leak that revealed tax evasion practices among the wealthy.

Archaeologists working near the West Link road construction in Inverness have discovered Bronze Age burnt mounds, kilns, and pottery fragments, providing insight into ancient practices such as heating water for potential cooking and other uses.
Main scored for the Latics after the hour mark, securing victory and maintaining Oldham's comfortable position above the League One relegation places.

The article reports the peaceful passing of Irish actor Lally, who had a successful career in film and television, including roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and Alexander, among other notable productions.

Derby City Council has agreed to keep Moorways Pool open for a year after initially planning to close it to save £350,000 annually, but its future remains uncertain pending a "fair deal" from central government.

The UN is concerned about the detention of children, reportedly from areas previously controlled by Boko Haram, in a military barracks in Maiduguri, Nigeria, citing a lack of proper legal process for civilians and children detained by the army.
Hearts head coach Robbie Neilson is considering signing experienced goalkeeper Lee Hollis, who recently became a free agent after leaving Motherwell, due to an injury to their current goalkeeper.

Korean basketball player Chelsey Lee, a US-born centre, is facing a lifetime suspension and annulled records after allegations surfaced that she and her agents fabricated her birth certificates to gain eligibility in the Women's Korean Basketball League.

A new app has been released by Ofcom to help people identify and troubleshoot issues with their wi-fi speeds, which coincides with research revealing that six million homes and offices in the UK are not achieving their full wi-fi potential.

Manchester United's Ibrahimovic and Pogba discussed the role of social media and pressure in football, with Ibrahimovic emphasizing that top players are not affected by external pressure and instead, put pressure on themselves to perform.

A metal object, later confirmed to be a payload shroud from the Alphasat satellite launched by the UK Space Agency and Arianespace in July, was found floating on a river in Brazil and is being collected by authorities.

Former Labour government minister James Purnell has warned that decriminalizing the non-payment of the TV licence fee could lead to increased non-payment, resulting in a £200m loss for the BBC and potentially forcing an increase in the licence fee.

Harps secured their first win over Derry since 1998 with a 2-1 victory at Finn Park, despite Rory Patterson scoring in injury-time, as they dominated the contest with former Derry players Barry Molloy and Tony McNamee impressing in midfield.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has announced that issuers of "distributed ledger or blockchain technology-based securities" must register their offers and sales, in an effort to protect investors and maintain market integrity amidst concerns over the potential investment bubble created by Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs).

Operation Anagram, a police investigation formed in 2006 by Strathclyde Police to track serial killer Peter Tobin, has led to the conviction of Tobin for the murders of three young women and continues to gather information and bring closure to families of potential victims.

At the Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel beat Lewis Hamilton's Mercedes, with both drivers expressing optimism about their chances in the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix, acknowledging the close competition and the need for continued improvement.
